newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.564 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.564 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate dipped to an average of 10.564 percent at Monday's regular weekly Treasury-bill auction from 10.625 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The other maturities also registered declines.
The 182-day T-bill rate nudged down to an average of 10.725 from 10.986 percent in the previous week; and the 364-day bill rate fell to 11.212 from 11.491 percent.
Traders said the high liquidity in the system led to the downward trend in interest rates as banks continued to shy away from term reverse repos which now carry a 20 percent tax.
The auction had tenders worth 23.715 billion pesos, of which 4.5 billion pesos were awarded.
A dealer said the decline in interest rates was also prodded by the Central Bank when it stopped offering its five-month special series T-bills which carried a rate of 10.90 percent.
"The Central Bank wanted the market to determine the rates at the auction," a foreign bank dealer said. The five-month bill had served as floor for banks when they bid for bills.
Among the maturities, the 364-day bills, which had sales of two billion pesos, generated the most number of tenders at 9.035 billion pesos.
This was followed by the 182-day bills with bids worth 8.210 billion pesos, of which 1.5 billion pesos were accepted.
The 91-day bills drew 6.470 billion pesos of bids, of which one billion pesos were accepted.
